title: Predictive coldstart cushion and isolation agreements — PRD draft
content:
Goal: sketch a product + operational approach that prevents latency spikes when dedicated pools see sudden warmup demand (cold-start waves, model cache misses, or new model versions), while preserving fair isolation and predictable economics for customers. This is a working PRD draft — exploratory, includes open questions and ops notes.

Context and motivation:
- Observed pain: spikes in tail latency and token-cost when dedicated pools import new models, encounter long KV-cache warming, or absorb burst traffic from a single noisy tenant. Existing burst credit pools reduce hard failures, but we still see 2-6× temporary cost and 3–10× tail latency for short windows (1–10m) on heavy models.
- Constraint: customers expect predictable billing & isolation guarantees. We cannot simply route all warmups to hosted spare capacity without explicit consent.
- Opportunity: combine short-term charged "cushions" (fast, ephemeral compute for warmups) with per-tenant soft isolation agreements and predictive warmup heuristics to reduce tail and cost impact.

User stories:
- Platform engineer: "I want dedicated pools to avoid 200–700ms extra tail latency during warmups for top-10 customers, without raising baseline cost."
- Tenant admin: "I want my reserved capacity not to be impacted by other tenants' cache churn, and to have transparent burst pricing for warmup compute."
- SRE oncall: "When a warmup wave hits, I want automated mitigation routes and a runbook that doesn't require manual scaling in 80% of cases."

Proposal overview (conceptual):
1) Predictive Coldstart Cushion (PCC) — ephemeral levy + warm lanes:
   - Maintain a small pool of hot-standby slots per region (policy-configurable per account tier). These slots are charged as a short-duration ephemeral add-on (metered at burst-warmup rate).
   - Use an ML-lite predictor (moving window + feature set: model version churn, recent request-to-model ratio, median input length, KV cache hit-rate) to detect imminent cold waves and pre-allocate cushions 30–90s ahead.
   - Cushions run the full model variant with a smaller batch target to warm KV caches and kernels; they are allowed to return partial early responses but must populate cache for tenant lanes.

2) Soft Isolation Agreements (SIA) — negotiated transient boundaries:
   - Each dedicated tenant has a soft ISO contract: baseline reserved capacity (hard), cushion allowance (soft ephemeral), and max-billable-burst (monetary cap).
   - During cushion-backed warmups, the platform enforces preferential warmlane affinity: cushion work warms KV on behalf of tenant-specific caches (not overlaying tenant X's cache with Y's data).
   - If a tenant exceeds their max-billable-burst, the system downgrades to a fallback variant (quantized or smaller context) with automatic notification and opt-in escalation channel.

3) Workload-aware heterogeneous-GPU allocation:
   - Avoid assigning cushion warmups to GPUs with poor kernel support for the model (e.g., older architectures or limited memory). Maintain a tiny metadata catalog for GPU families and per-model warmup efficiency multiplier.
   - The allocator uses GPU-family-aware scoring so warmups land on nodes with known faster kernel ramps.

4) Billing & economics:
   - Cushion minutes are metered separately under a descriptive line item: "warmup cushion (per-tenant)" with a rate between on-demand and reserved (reflects extra operational burden).
   - For burst-free customers, option to pre-purchase cushion credits at discount. Unused credits roll forward for a short window.

Operational flows and runbook snippets:
- Normal predictive flow: predictor flags model X as showing churn pattern -> pre-allocates 10 cushion slots for tenant A -> cushions run short-fused warmup workload and push KV fingerprints into cache -> baseline perf holds, cushion tasks terminate.
- Reactive fallback: sudden unexpected wave without prediction -> platform attempts immediate cushion allocation (best-effort) -> if insufficient capacity, apply lane fallback (quantized model) for non-critical requests and route critical requests to high-priority lane (if tenant has paid for it).
- Lossy failure case: cushion hotpool saturates -> apply rate-limiter and queued warm requests with SLA-graded timeouts; alert SRE and auto-open DED-1423-style incident if tail-latency > 2× SLA for >5min.

Metrics to track (proposal):
- Warmup tail-latency (p95/p99 for first 30s after cold model activation) per-tenant.
- Cushion efficacy: percent reduction in p99 when cushion used vs control windows.
- Cushion allocation success ratio (predictive allocations that completed before first large request).
- Cost delta: cushion-minutes billed vs baseline token-cost increase avoided.
- Cache priming hit-rate within 60s of cushion completion.

Implementation sketch (phased):
Phase 0 (experiment, 2–4 weeks):
- Lightweight predictor: heuristic using moving averages (cache-miss rate > threshold OR new model version deploy count > N in last T minutes).
- Single-region cushion pool (modifiable via infra flag). Manual billing attribution (ops tag).
- Basic runbook and Slack notifications to SRE.
Phase 1 (productize, 8–12 weeks):
- ML-lite predictor retraining and continuous evaluation.
- Per-tenant cushion quotas & API to opt-in/out; admin UI toggle in Console.
- Billing hookup with metering and line-item generation.
Phase 2 (optimization, 12+ weeks):
- GPU-family catalog + allocator integration.
- Soft Isolation Agreements formalized in contract templates and automated enforcement.
- Pre-purchase credit flow and conservative chargeback UX.

Security & compliance considerations:
- Cushion warmup tasks must not persist tenant data beyond necessary cache fingerprinting. Ensure ephemeral tasks respect data residency settings (no cross-region warmups unless tenant allows).
- Audit logs: every cushion allocation should record source predictor signal, GPU node id, model variant used, and billing tag.

Open questions / risks (to discuss):
- Pricing sensitivity: how many customers will accept explicit warmup charges vs. prefer fixed higher reserve pricing?
- Predictor mistakes: false positives (wasted cushion minutes) vs false negatives (miss warmups). Cost tradeoffs need experiments.
- Cache semantics: how to ensure cushion-populated cache entries are usable by tenant lanes without leaking cross-tenant artifacts? Need infra experiment on strict cache partitioning.
- Legal: need Product Legal to sign off on per-burst-line items and how they interact with existing Dedicated contracts (enterprise customers may require amendment).

Next steps / action items:
- [Maya] set up quick A/B test on 2 customers with predictable churn patterns (approx 10% traffic) to measure p99 improvement. Track outcome for 2 weeks. (Jira: DED-1423)
- [Arjun] prototype a one-region cushion controller and add a Slack alert channel for cushion exhaust.
- [Lina] draft a short Console UI mock for "cushion opt-in / caps" and sample contract language for SIAs.
- [Ethan] design a cache-partition experiment to validate no cross-tenant leakage during cushion warming.

Notes to self / rough heuristics: 
- Cushion size initially: 1–3 slots per 100 reserved GPUs for tier-1, scaled down for lower tiers. Tune hard.
- Warmup batch target: 1/2 of steady-state batch size to avoid interfering with live traffic on shared nodes.
- Metric latency window: treat first 90s as warm window for measurement.

References and related tickets:
- DED-1423 (warmup cushion A/B test)
- Infra PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987 (prototype allocator changes)
- Confluence: Coldstart Playbook (linked)

Appendix: quick FAQ (for internal review)
Q: Why not use existing burst credits?
A: Burst credits help with capacity but do not target model cache warmups or GPU-family warm allocations; cushions are explicitly tuned to pre-populate KV and kernels.
Q: Do we force customers onto cushions?
A: No. Default behavior for existing customers is no charge. Product teams should offer opt-in with trial credits for early adopters.
Q: How to measure success?
A: Aim for >50% reduction in p99 for warm windows with <10% increase in billed compute due to cushions for initial trials.

— end of draft —
